concepts.def: The right amounts of carbohydrate, protein, lipid, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.
Breaking large insoluble food molecules into small soluble ones.
Small soluble molecules pass into the blood through the small intestine.
Finger-like folds that increase the surface area for absorption.
Made in the liver; emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Human Nutrition — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Human Nutrition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Human Nutrition.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: What is the main role of B-cells compared to T-cells?
options: T-cells produce antibodies and B-cells kill infected cells.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
B-cells and T-cells both produce antibodies in equal amounts.
B-cells produce antibodies (humoral response); T-cells coordinate the immune response and kill infected cells (cell-mediated response).

mcqs.q: How do vaccines protect you from a disease?
options: They expose your immune system to a harmless form of the pathogen so memory cells form, allowing rapid response if exposed later.
Vaccines kill the pathogen if it ever enters the body.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
T-cells produce antibodies and B-cells kill infected cells.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell”?
options: Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Subcellular structures”?
options: Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
